analysis.summary: Petro Carbon and Chemicals Limited reported its financial and operational performance for FY25, highlighting stable production volumes despite material price headwinds and margin compression. Management discussed strategic expansions, including the commissioning of a 10 MW WHRB power plant, environmental clearance for capacity expansion, and the incorporation of new subsidiaries to strengthen backward integration. The company maintains a strong B2B customer base across the aluminium and steel industries, supported by its strategically located manufacturing plant. Petro Carbon and Chemicals Limited reported a significant increase in financial performance for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with turnover reaching Rs. 57,665.15 lakhs compared to Rs.

guidance.claim: Petro Carbon plans to use Heavy Creosote Oil in place of Furnace Oil during production to achieve cost savings.
guidance.quote: Future plan of action : The Company is planning to use Heavy Creosote Oil in place of Furnace Oil during production.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that the fortune of the CPC industry is closely linked with the fortune of the aluminium industry.
demand_outlook.quote: Fortune of CPC industry is closely linked with the fortune of aluminium industry

demand_outlook.claim: Financial year 2025 experienced pricing pressures and reduced sales volumes across operations.
demand_outlook.quote: FY25 witnessed a drop in sales volumes and pricing pressure, affecting overall segment performance.

capex_expansion.claim: PCCL commissioned a 10 MW WHRB Power Plant at Haldia Oil Refinery.
capex_expansion.quote: Haldia Oil Refinery, Haldia – 10 MW WHRB Power Plant

capex_expansion.claim: Petro Carbon commissioned a 10 MW power plant at its Haldia factory on March 6, 2025, with a capital expenditure of Rs. 7,111.77 lakhs.
capex_expansion.quote: During the FY 2024-25, 10 Mega Watt Power Plant was commissioned at the Haldia Factory of the Company on 6th March, 2025 and the Company has incurred Capital Expenditure of Rs.7,111.77 lakhs for the same.

capex_expansion.claim: The company received approval for an expansion project at Haldia comprising an Electrically Calcined Anthracite Plant, Coal Tar Distillation Plant, and revamping of its Old Carbon Paste Plant.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company has got approval of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, vide their letter dated 23rd April, 2025, for proposed expansion project of the existing plant located in Haldia, West Bengal by installation of 72,000 TPA Electrically Calcined Anthracite Plant, 60,000 TPA Coal Tar Distillation Plant and 48,000 TPA by revamping of Old Carbon Paste Plant.

margins_costs.claim: Management stated that the CPC industry faced headwinds in FY 2025 primarily due to elevated raw material prices which resulted in margin compression.
margins_costs.quote: The CPC industry faced headwinds in FY 2025, primarily due to elevated raw material prices. These increases could not be fully passed on to customers, resulting in margin compression and a weakened bottom line across the sector.

margins_costs.claim: The decline in FY2025 revenue and profit was mainly driven by a reduction in Calcined Petroleum Coke market prices.
margins_costs.quote: The sharp decline in revenue and profit during FY2025 was primarily due to a decrease in the market price of Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC).

orders_capacity.claim: The CPC plant has an installed capacity of approximately 93,744 tons per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: The Plant has a capacity of approximately 93,744 tons per annum of CPC and the plant comprises an area of around 30 acres with good infrastructure facilities like own railway sliding inside the plant premises itself facilitating unloading / loading of wagons, along with yard / shed to store both Raw Petroleum Coke (RPC) / Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC).

orders_capacity.claim: Petro Carbon produced 84,305.500 MT of Calcined Petroleum Coke in FY 2024-25 compared to 91,541.200 MT in FY 2023-24.
orders_capacity.quote: Production of CPC for fiscal year 2024-25 was 84,305.500 MT against 91,541.200 MT in financial year 2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: The Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year under review in order to conserve resources for future expansion and working capital requirements.
capital_allocation.quote: In order to conserve resources for future expansion and working capital requirements, your Directors have decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year under review.

capital_allocation.claim: The company did not transfer any amount to reserves during the year under review.
capital_allocation.quote: No amount has been transferred to the reserves by the Board during the year under review.

risks_headwinds.claim: The industry faces heavy reliance on imports such as low-sulphur RPC from the U.S. and other Europe and Asian countries affecting cost and availability.
risks_headwinds.quote: Heavy reliance on imports (esp. low-sulphur RPC from the U.S. and Other Europe and Asian countries) affects cost and availability.

risks_headwinds.claim: The energy-intensive calcination process raises operational costs during power and fuel inflation.
risks_headwinds.quote: Energy-intensive calcination process raises operational costs, especially during power/fuel inflation.

risks_headwinds.claim: Trade restrictions and anti-dumping duties or export/import restrictions in key markets impact pricing.
risks_headwinds.quote: Anti-dumping duties or export/import restrictions in key markets (e.g., China, USA and West Asia Market) impact pricing.

risks_headwinds.claim: Petro Carbon faces foreign exchange risk as it imports over 90% of its raw materials.
risks_headwinds.quote: The company imports more than 90% of its raw materials from foreign suppliers as a result of which the company faces foreign exchange risk.

risks_headwinds.claim: Imported raw petroleum coke costs are subject to international crude oil prices, stock levels at refineries, and shipping costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: Cost of these imported RPCs are dependent on cost of international crude oil, stock of RPCs in various refineries and shipping cost.

management_commitments.claim: Petro Carbon plans to use Heavy Creosote Oil in place of Furnace Oil during production.
management_commitments.quote: Future plan of action : The Company is planning to use Heavy Creosote Oil in place of Furnace Oil during production.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
